item.title: Sophie Weston Chien in conversation with Natalia Duong & Akshita Sivakumar — Mon Oct 5, 4:45 PM — Cruess Hall
item.description:
This conversation will build off Weston Chien’s recent series Touching Toxicity, a body of textile work that maps contamination and remediation across the East Bay. Industrial heavy metals and volatile organic compounds have contaminated the soil and groundwater of the Bay Area, an issue made even more fraught when rising sea levels can push these materials further to the surface. Environmental remediation often focuses on removing the harm wrought by toxicity; sites are returned to a pre-toxic state through the removal or capping of harmful materials. Touching Toxicity considers what a framework of return means given larger and longer trends of environmental harm. Together, the panelists will discuss toxicity, remediation, and how artistic and design practice might offer new timescales and tactics for environmental justice.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Reflecting Images: Christianity and AI in Conversation — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — The Episcopal Church of St. Martin
item.description: The conversation about artificial intelligence, or AI, has become a significant part of our everyday lives, to the point that so much of the current economy is bound up in this technology. It’s hard to listen to a newscast or read a headline without some mention of AI, either as ground-breaking technology that will make our lives easier and more efficient, or as a possible threat to human existence. Three local pastors have come together out of the belief that “people of faith ought to be able to think and speak intelligently about AI and navigate the many issues it involves while holding onto the values that guide them in their faith,” according to Mae Forrest Barnes, Ph.D., an Episocpalian with a background in theology and ethics and a special focus in accessibility, science, and theological ethics. item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Oct 4, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Rotary Club of Davis Centennial Celebration — Sun Oct 4, 5:00 PM — Veterans Memorial Theatre
item.description: Rotary Club of Davis to celebrate 100 years of service The Rotary Club of Davis will mark its centennial with a community celebration from 5 to 8 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, at the Davis Veterans Memorial Center. Founded in 1926 under the auspices of Rotary International, the Rotary Club of Davis has spent a century combining service, fellowship and civic involvement. The original Davis club is now one of three Rotary clubs in the city, along with Sunrise Rotary Club of Davis and Sunset Rotary Club of Davis. Tickets for the centennial dinner are $45 and include dinner by Simply Satisfied Catering. For tickets, contact Donna Prebys at 630-803-7954. Dave Scheiber will serve as master of ceremonies. The evening’s program will include a presentation on a century of Davis Rotary by Michael Peterson and Jonathan Bayless, a Rotary trivia contest led by Bruce and Marjorie Hartsough, and remarks about the club’s future from Prebys, the club’s 2026-27 president. item.description:

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Oct 21, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Author talk by Peter Flax: Why We Ride — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.

item.title: Mondavi Event: Galactic — Thu Oct 29, 7:30 PM — Mondavi Center
item.description:
Join GSP for a special event at the Mondavi Center. For more than 30 years, Galactic has been a powerhouse of New Orleans music, fusing funk, jazz, rock, hip-hop and soul into a sound unmistakably their own. From late-night funk outfit to genre-defying collective, Galactic brings their electrifying live performance to Jackson Hall. Joined by powerhouse vocalist Anjelika “Jelly” Joseph, expect a night of fresh energy, soulful vocals, and an expansive, high-octane sound.
Tickets are limited to 20 students. First come, first serve. A confirmation email will be sent out during week 2 of the event. You MUST confirm your attendance no later than Thursday, October 15 or you can lose your seat. You are welcomed to bring a friend (Non-GSP student) but please reach out if your friend is not able to make it so we can distribute tickets for other students.
Tickets must be claimed by October 15th.
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout – Monthly Downtown Davis Art Walk (Free!) — Fri Dec 11, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Join Davis’s beloved 2nd Friday ArtAbout – a free monthly self-guided artwalk coordinated by the Pence Gallery! Every second Friday, stroll downtown Davis to discover fresh exhibits, opening receptions, live music, hands-on activities, and direct chats with local and regional artists at 10+ galleries, co-ops, and businesses. Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. Many venues offer complimentary refreshments like wine and snacks. Free – no tickets required!
Runs approximately 5:00–9:00 PM (venue receptions vary—check the monthly guide for specifics). Grab the printed guide (with map & details) the week of at the Pence Gallery or participating spots, or download it at pencegallery.org/events/artabout/.
